getStateAttributesProps(state, customMap.type: <State extends Record<string, any>>(state: State, customMapping?: StateAttributesMapping<State>) => Record<string, string>
getStateAttributesProps(state, customMap.semantic: Turns a component state object into the data-* attribute map; keys present with falsy/false values are dropped, truthy booleans become empty-string attributes.

StateAttributesMapping<State>.type: { [K in keyof State]?: (value: State[K]) => Record<string, string> | null }
StateAttributesMapping<State>.semantic: Per-key override returning an attribute map (or null to emit nothing).

transitionStatusMapping.semantic: Ships the data-starting-style / data-ending-style mapping used by animating parts (Tabs.Panel among them).

renderProp: Both `useRender` and the internal `useRenderElement` accept a `stateAttributesMapping` parameter, so author components can emit custom data-* attributes from their state without hand-writing attribute JSX. This is the sanctioned way to give a migrated component stable data-* hooks that replaced React Aria's data-selected/data-hovered etc.
notableDifferences: React Aria generates data-* attributes internally with no public mapping API; Base UI exposes one, which is the migration lever for preserving consumer CSS that keyed off RAC attributes — map your own state onto the historical attribute names (e.g. emit data-selected yourself) instead of rewriting downstream styles.
Transition attributes are the one animation contract that differs in name only from React Aria's entering/exiting conventions: Base UI uses data-starting-style/data-ending-style.
